source.title: BLUEFIN: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Financial Spreadsheets

candidates.name: rubric-based evaluation
candidates.summary: Evaluating complex outputs by checking them against a set of fine-grained, usually binary, criteria with assigned point weights, and aggregating the weighted points met. It suits tasks that are hard to verify with a single programmatic test.
candidates.evidence: 3,225 granular rubric criteria

candidates.name: LLM-as-a-judge
candidates.summary: Using a language model to grade other models' outputs against a rubric or reference, sometimes with tools to inspect the artifact. Its reliability is usually checked by comparing its judgments with human labels.
candidates.evidence: can be reliably evaluated by an LM judge agent

candidates.name: benchmark
candidates.summary: A standardized set of tasks and scoring procedures used to measure and compare the capabilities of models or systems on a defined skill area.

candidates.name: LLM agent
candidates.summary: A language model that works toward a goal by repeatedly choosing and calling tools, observing the results, and deciding what to do next until it signals completion.
candidates.evidence: tasks large language model (LLM) agents

candidates.name: agent harness
candidates.summary: The software layer around a model that supplies its tools, prompts, observation handling and termination logic, so that model behavior can be run and compared in a controlled environment.
candidates.evidence: an agentic harness of 20 tools organized into six categories

candidates.name: inter-annotator agreement
candidates.summary: The degree to which independent human raters assign the same labels to the same items. It is used to establish a reliability ceiling and to validate automated judges.
candidates.evidence: inter-annotator alignment study over 384 binary criteria

candidates.name: Krippendorff's alpha
candidates.summary: A chance-corrected reliability coefficient for agreement among raters that works with different data types and missing ratings. A value of 1 means perfect agreement and 0 means chance-level agreement.
candidates.evidence: Krippendorff's Alpha of 0.826

candidates.name: macro-averaged F1 score
candidates.summary: The F1 score, the harmonic mean of precision and recall, computed separately for each class and then averaged with equal weight per class. It treats rare and common classes equally.
candidates.evidence: macro F1 score of 0.839

candidates.name: perturbation testing
candidates.summary: Changing a driving input of a model and checking that dependent outputs recompute to the correct new values. It detects hardcoded values and broken formula links that look correct under the original inputs.
candidates.evidence: A perturbation criterion specifies an input mutation

candidates.name: spreadsheet formula dependency
candidates.summary: Spreadsheet cells reference other cells so that changes propagate through chains of calculations. Linking to a single authoritative source cell, rather than hardcoding or recomputing values locally, keeps a model dynamic and auditable.
candidates.evidence: dense, graph-structured dependencies

candidates.name: hardcoded value
candidates.summary: A constant typed directly into a cell or formula where a formula or reference should supply the value. It breaks the model's dynamic behavior when inputs change.
candidates.evidence: Do not hardcode computed values when a formula can produce the result.

candidates.name: discounted cash flow valuation
candidates.summary: A valuation method that projects a company's future free cash flows and discounts them to present value using a discount rate, adding a discounted terminal value to estimate enterprise value.
candidates.evidence: value the company using a DCF

candidates.name: weighted average cost of capital
candidates.summary: The blended required return of a firm's debt and equity financing, weighted by their proportions in the capital structure. It is commonly used as the discount rate in DCF valuation.
candidates.evidence: change WACC from 8.5% to 10%

candidates.name: leveraged buyout model
candidates.summary: A financial model of acquiring a company largely with debt, including sources and uses of funds, debt schedules and returns to equity investors. It often involves circular references such as interest depending on cash sweep.
candidates.evidence: debt schedules and LBO-style circular references converge correctly

candidates.name: circular reference
candidates.summary: A spreadsheet situation where a cell's formula depends, directly or indirectly, on its own result. It requires iterative calculation to converge to a stable value.
candidates.evidence: iterative-calc enabled

candidates.name: debt schedule
candidates.summary: A model section that tracks beginning balances, repayments, cash sweeps, interest and ending balances for each debt tranche over time, often including a revolver that covers cash shortfalls.
candidates.evidence: Build a debt schedule section at the bottom of the uploaded worksheet

candidates.name: three-statement financial model
candidates.summary: An integrated model projecting the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement from assumptions, with the balance sheet required to balance in every period.
candidates.evidence: A Check line equal to Total Assets minus Total Equity and Liabilities

candidates.name: financial modeling best practices
candidates.summary: Conventions for building clear, auditable spreadsheet models, such as separating inputs from calculations, avoiding hardcodes, and using consistent formatting like blue font for hardcoded assumptions.
candidates.evidence: standard financial modeling conventions [20]

candidates.name: Pareto frontier
candidates.summary: The set of options for which no other option is both cheaper and better. Options off the frontier are dominated by at least one frontier option.
candidates.evidence: The Pareto frontier traces Grok 4.20 → Gemini 3.1 Pro → GPT-5.5

candidates.name: programmatic verifiability
candidates.summary: The property of a task whose outputs can be checked by executable tests or exact-match comparison. Tasks with subjective or multi-dimensional quality criteria are hard to verify this way.
candidates.evidence: difficult to verify programmatically

candidates.name: sandboxed code execution
candidates.summary: Running model-written code in a restricted environment with limited built-ins, allow-listed imports, no file or network access and a timeout, to limit risk while allowing bulk operations.
candidates.evidence: restricted built-ins and a tight import whitelist (no file I/O, no network)

candidates.name: minimal-elicitation prompting
candidates.summary: Giving a model a very short prompt with no workflow prescriptions or tool preferences, so that evaluation reflects the model's own capability rather than how well it follows detailed instructions.
candidates.evidence: minimal-elicitation prompt (61 words

candidates.name: benchmark data leakage
candidates.summary: The risk that benchmark items appear in training data, inflating scores. Keeping a private held-out set while releasing a public one mitigates it.
candidates.evidence: We retain a private set primarily out of potential leakage concerns

candidates.name: reasoning effort setting
candidates.summary: A model API parameter controlling how much internal reasoning computation the model spends before responding. Scales are not comparable across providers.
candidates.evidence: All models are set to high reasoning via their respective provider APIs

resolutions.name: benchmark
resolutions.reason: A generic benchmark is a broader concept than contamination, agent benchmarks, or verifiability, none of which is the same idea.

shortlist.name: Benchmark data leakage and held-out sets

resolutions.reason: Same name, aliases and definition of agreement among independent raters.

resolutions.name: hardcoded value
resolutions.reason: Both define hardcoding as typing a constant where a formula should supply the value.

resolutions.name: leveraged buyout model
resolutions.reason: Identical concept: the leveraged buyout (LBO) model of a debt-financed acquisition.
